results.summary: Keep this as the North Fork Quinault approach — the standard way in, and the one its trailhead, map pins and route breakdown already use — and rewrite the day plan, published times, road card and tips that described the Elwha side (whose road to the trailhead is still closed at Madison Falls).
results.evidence: The park's North Fork Quinault trail page gives 16 miles from the trailhead (519 ft) to Low Divide (3,602 ft), with fords at Wild Rose Creek, Elip Creek and Sixteen Mile and camps at Wolf Bar, Elip Creek, Trapper, Sixteen Mile and Low Divide; a club route listing describes Mount Seattle as a 19-mile approach up the North Fork of the Quinault. On the Elwha side, park road status and a hiking guide both say Olympic Hot Springs Road and Whiskey Bend Road are closed to vehicles, with a 6.2-mile one-way road walk from Madison Falls, so the old Elwha day plan (starting at Whiskey Bend) described a start nobody can drive to. The park's road page lists North Shore Road and the North Fork Quinault Road open (May 2026), reachable from North Shore Road only while South Shore Road is washed out. No source gives per-day miles, gain or hours for the Quinault side, so the new day plan carries no day figures except the unchanged summit day (camp to summit and back), and the Elwha-derived approach/descent/total hours are nulled rather than replaced. The approach prose, which presents both sides as options, is left as it is. NOT changed and worth an owner look: dist_km 98.17 (the old 61-mile Elwha round trip, stored as if one-way) and gain_ft 7500 — no two sources state a Quinault figure (one club listing gives 19 mi one-way and 5,750 ft gain).

expect.cal: Olympic National Park wilderness permits (quota-based in summer) are required for all backcountry camps along this route; check current NPS conditions reports for Elwha River Trail bridge/washout status before committing to the approach.

results.summary: Stop saying the first ascent was made with Bill Thomas or at 5.9: the one detailed history says the father stayed in camp and the first ascent used short aid, so the text now just names Kearney and Thomas, matching the first-ascent line.
results.evidence: A route history names the party as Alan Kearney and Jeff Thomas (August 1984), with Jeff's father Bill Thomas on the trip but staying in camp, and describes the first ascent as using two short aid sections (graded 5.11b or 5.10b C1) — contradicting the beta's 'with Jeff and Bill Thomas' and its 'first climbed as a six-pitch Grade III 5.9 route'. A route database lists the first ascent only as 'Kearney, Thomas' (two climbers), and the AAJ south-face topo calls it Kearney-Thomas (III 5.11). No second source gives first names or the year, so the fa column ('Kearney and Thomas (first names and date unknown)') is left and the beta is brought into line with it: Bill is removed, and the unsupported original pitch count/grade and 'free-climbed harder' history are dropped. The current 5.11a grade is unchanged.

results.summary: The walk in is about 2.5 miles each way (about 5 miles round trip); the stored approach distance held the round trip in the one-way slot, so it now says 2.5 miles one way (4.0 km) and the day plan says 5 miles round trip.
results.evidence: A trail-map record gives 2.5 mi one way from the Blue Lake Trailhead to the Early Winters Spires, and an independent South Early Winters Spire write-up from the same trailhead gives 5 miles round trip. dist_km is read as one-way (the app doubles it for the round trip), so the stored 8.37 km showed roughly twice the real walk; neighbouring South Early Winters Spire rows (South Arete, Northwest Face) already store 4.0 km. The itinerary's 5.2 mi round trip is set to the 5 mi both sources state so the two fields agree. Gain is not changed (no source states one for this route).
